name: Burn
label: Revelation
lede: Burn put four songs on one Revelation seven-inch in 1990, with a swing and a stop-start menace New York hardcore hadn't heard, then waited twenty-seven years for a full-length.

eras.title: Fire and fusion on four songs
eras.text: By 1989 the youth crew sound had hardened into a formula. Gavin Van Vlack, out of Side by Side and Absolution, wanted a band that swung, and Chaka Malik could ride it. One seven-inch later, New York hardcore had a new way to move.

years.src: No Echo: Chaka Malik interview · The Hundreds
years.h: Gavin Van Vlack wants a hardcore band that swings
years.p: Van Vlack recruits singer [[Chaka Malik|072518f3-a3d6-40af-8d5a-9f30d25de77e]], drummer [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] of Beyond and bassist Alex Napack of [[Pressure Release|d129edff-83d0-4d95-976c-87b6a2dd57fd]], who names the band.
years.xp:
Malik told No Echo it was Van Vlack who said, "We're gonna get you a band." The Hundreds has Van Vlack saying Malik "was into a lot of different things that no one else was listening to."

Drummer John Krisciun played with Burn before Cage.

years.big: "It was so lawless, that you could really do anything."
years.h: Burn rehearses in Williamsburg and plays the Lower East Side
years.p: Gavin Van Vlack on New York at the time. Burn rehearses in South Williamsburg and plays CBGB, the Pyramid Club and ABC No Rio.
years.xp:
Van Vlack's road to Burn was rough. He told No Echo his family moved to New York from New Hampshire when his mother needed cancer treatment at Sloan Kettering; he landed in foster care, and from 15 on he slept in abandoned buildings and on friends' floors, with [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] sometimes sneaking him into his parents' house.

Before hardcore there was graffiti: he wrote NATZ with the SPORTS crew in the eighties. The son of a Mexican mother and a Dutch father, he's said both sides of the family were hostile to the mix. That street-level looseness came onto the stage with him.

years.src: Revelation Records · RevHQ Speak Up · The Hundreds
years.h: The Burn 7" swings where other records sprint
years.p: Revelation No. 22 has four songs, among them Shall Be Judged, an animal-rights sermon in Malik's delivery. Writer Anthony Pappalardo heard fire and fusion, pounding the pavement like demo-era [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]].
years.xp:
What set it apart was the rhythm: swing and sudden dynamic drops where other bands just went faster. Pappalardo says Drown took "more from Joni Mitchell than Tony Iommi", with some Sabbath in the gene pool anyway.

Malik came up with the cover concept, and Revelation's own page calls the record groundbreaking. Revelation's catalog lists a first run split between black and pink vinyl, and it has been repressed ever since. The band's full 27-minute set from January 12, 1991 is on video.

years.h: Alan Cage joins Quicksand, and the search for his replacement stalls
years.p: The drummer goes to [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]]' new band. Burn can't find anyone who plays at his level.
years.xp: Malik told No Echo: "Alan left to join Quicksand and we had a hard time finding a drummer that could play at his level."

eras.title: Greenpoint, and a record that waited a decade
eras.text: Without Cage the band kept writing, moved to Greenpoint, and recorded in 1992. Then it ended, and the members scattered into the noisier, heavier bands of the nineties.

years.h: Burn ends, and its members scatter into heavier bands
years.p: Chaka Malik starts [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]]. Gavin Van Vlack goes on to [[Die 116|59ff819b-b635-473d-ba52-f61d44835bd7]], Pry and The Big Collapse.
years.xp: Van Vlack told The Hundreds: "When we broke up, things were going fairly well, but there was tension." Wikipedia dates the split to 1992; The Hundreds says only the early nineties. A full set from June 21, 1991, at the Marquee in New York, shows the band a year before the end.

eras.title: Cleanse
eras.text: A short return in 1998 grew into a new line-up with Vic DiCara, of Inside Out and 108, on second guitar. Two releases came out of it, one brand new, one ten years old.

years.h: Burn plays again for the first time since 1992
years.p: A short return that grows into a new line-up by 2001, with [[Vic DiCara|a6698e1f-db17-4e93-9c4f-56678238e91f]] on second guitar.

years.h: Live at Coney Island High, NYC, December 30, 1997
yt: Live at Coney Island High, NYC, December 30, 1997

years.h: Cleanse brings a second guitarist and a new bassist
years.p: Chaka Malik and Gavin Van Vlack are joined by Vic DiCara on guitar and Manny Carrero, later of [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], on bass. The EP is on Equal Vision.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the EP as a late 2001 release on Equal Vision, with DiCara arriving from [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] and [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].

years.h: Revelation digs out Burn's last session
years.p: Burn taped it in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, in 1992, just before breaking up. It comes out ten years later as Last Great Sea.
years.xp: Malik told No Echo the band had just moved into a new Greenpoint apartment, and that "everything was new... nothing was established so that's always part of the DNA."

eras.title: The word is real
eras.text: Twenty-five years after the seven-inch, Burn came back as a working band, not a reunion act: new players, new records, and in 2017 the first full-length the band had ever made.

years.cap: Burn live, crowd at the stage, March 5, 2016
q: The word that comes to mind, is real.
years.src: No Echo: Chaka Malik interview · The Hundreds
years.h: Burn comes back at the Black N' Blue Bowl
years.p: Burn is added as an exclusive appearance at the New York hardcore festival's May weekend, with [[Durijah Lang|42c3124a-fa12-4e3f-a373-6bc155dd416f]] on drums and Manny Carrero on bass.
years.xp: No Echo has Sacha Jenkins talking Malik into the reunion, and puts the set on May 17. Malik said the plan was to play more in the style of the original four-song 1990 seven-inch than the later records.

years.h: Burn plays London, then three nights in California
years.p: London on October 4, then Santa Ana, Berkeley and Los Angeles from October 9 to 11. The full Berkeley set at 924 Gilman is on video.

years.cap: Burn live, the pit during the set, March 5, 2016
years.h: From the Ashes is the first new Burn since 2001
years.p: Bridge 9 puts out the EP, fifteen years after Cleanse.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the EP announced in April 2016. A full set from August 4, 2016 is on video.

years.cap: Chaka Malik singing with Burn, Persistence Tour, Munich, January 25, 2017
years.h: Twenty-eight years in, Burn makes a full-length
years.p: Do or Die comes out on Deathwish Inc., produced by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] and mastered by Howie Weinberg.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the 2017 line-up as Malik, Van Vlack, Tyler Krupsky on bass and Abbas Muhammad on drums.
